questions.q: What is the key difference between synchronous and asynchronous Apex execution?
options: Synchronous code runs immediately in the calling transaction; asynchronous code is handed off to run later in its own transaction
Asynchronous code always runs faster than synchronous code
There is no real difference — both run in the same transaction at the same time
Synchronous code can only be triggered by a button click, asynchronous code cannot
questions.explain: Synchronous Apex runs on the spot in the caller's transaction, which waits for it. Asynchronous Apex is queued and run later by the platform in its own transaction with fresh governor limits.

questions.q: Which four tools does this course cover as ways to run Apex asynchronously?
options: Triggers, Visualforce, Lightning Web Components, and SOQL
Future methods, Queueable Apex, Batch Apex, and Scheduled Apex
Validation Rules, Flows, Process Builder, and Workflow Rules
Change Sets, Scratch Orgs, Packages, and Unlocked Packages
questions.explain: The four asynchronous Apex tools are future methods, Queueable Apex, Batch Apex, and Scheduled Apex — each suited to a different kind of problem, covered in Lessons 3 through 6.

questions.q: What does the AsyncApexJob object track?
options: Only the results of SOQL queries run in synchronous transactions
The status, type, and progress of every future method call, Queueable job, Batch Apex job, and Scheduled Apex execution
User login history and session information
Validation rule error messages shown to end users
questions.explain: Every asynchronous job — future, Queueable, Batch, or Scheduled Apex — creates a row in AsyncApexJob, tracking fields like Status, JobType, NumberOfErrors, and TotalJobItems.

questions.q: Why is it a mistake to assume an asynchronous job runs the instant it's queued?
options: Asynchronous jobs never actually run unless manually triggered from Setup
The platform queues and runs asynchronous work when capacity allows, honoring shared org-wide limits — not necessarily the instant it's submitted
Asynchronous jobs only run once a day, at midnight
Asynchronous jobs require a human to click an 'Approve' button before they execute
questions.explain: Queuing asynchronous work means the platform will run it when it can, respecting org capacity and the shared daily async limits — usually within seconds, but never guaranteed to the instant.

questions.q: A trigger needs to make an HTTP callout to an external service. Why can't this run synchronously inside the trigger?
options: Callouts aren't allowed from synchronous contexts like triggers, so the work must be handed off to an asynchronous tool
Triggers are not allowed to contain any Apex code at all
HTTP callouts are only possible from Scheduled Apex
Callouts can run synchronously in a trigger with no restrictions
questions.explain: Salesforce doesn't allow direct callouts from triggers (or other synchronous contexts that run as part of a DML transaction) — this is one of the concrete reasons asynchronous Apex exists, covered further in Lesson 2.
